A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ifosfamide is a prodrug that is activated in vivo by cytochrome P450 2B1 to form the highly reactive metabolites 4-hydroxyifosfamide and 4-hydroperoxyifosfamide, which then spontaneously decompose to yield acrolein, chloracetaldehyde, 2-chloroacetaldehyde, and 2-chlorohydrin.
the urinary excretion of neurotoxic metabolites of ifosfamide (IFO) is increased in children with the GSTM1 null genotype.

the urinary excretion of neurotoxic side chain metabolites (NSCM) of ifosfamide (IFO) is higher in children with the GSTM1 null and GSTT1 null genotypes than in children with GSTM1 and GSTT1 active genotypes.

there is a significant difference in the excretion of the metabolites of ifosfamide, which is neurotoxic, in children with polymorphisms of the glutathiones S-transferases genes.
